subtopics.title: Question One — Concepts and the Asset Disposal

questions.question: A vehicle costing R180 000 is depreciated at 20 percent on cost and sold nine months into the year. The current-year depreciation is:
options: R27 000 — R36 000 apportioned for nine months
R36 000 — a full year regardless of the sale date

questions.question: Accumulated depreciation is R100 800 plus R27 000 for the current year. The carrying value at sale is:
options: R52 200 — cost of R180 000 minus R127 800

questions.question: The concept that forbids overstating income or assets is:
In the time-apportionment step, the mark most often lost comes from:
options: Charging a full year of depreciation instead of the months that actually ran

questions.question: Rent of R78 000 was received for thirteen months. The year's rent income and the deferral are:
options: R72 000 income; R6 000 income received in advance

questions.question: Insurance of R14 400 includes three months belonging to next year. The adjustment is:
options: Subtract R3 600 from the expense and show a prepaid expense of R3 600
Ignore it — insurance is always a full-year cost

questions.question: A R600 000 loan at 10 percent shows interest of only R55 000 recorded. The correction is:
options: Accrue a further R5 000 so the expense reaches R60 000

questions.question: Net profit before tax is R720 000. The tax line, at the company rate, is:
options: R194 400 at twenty-seven percent, leaving R525 600 after tax

subtopics.title: The Share Capital and Retained Income Notes

questions.question: After issuing 100 000 shares at R6,00 onto an opening R2 800 000 for 700 000 shares, the new average issue price is:
Fifty thousand shares are repurchased at R5,05 against a R4,25 average. The share capital note shows:
options: R212 500 out — fifty thousand at the average; the 80 cents premium goes to retained income

questions.question: The interim dividend used 800 000 shares but the final used 750 000 because:
options: The buy-back happened between the two dividends, so fewer shares remained for the final

questions.question: Opening retained income R410 000, profit after tax R525 600, buy-back premium R40 000, dividends R540 000. Closing retained income:
SARS for income tax appears in current liabilities at R14 400 because:
options: The charge of R194 400 exceeds provisional payments of R180 000 by that amount
It is the full tax charge

questions.question: The tenant's extra month of rent lands on the balance sheet as:
options: Income received in advance of R6 000 in current liabilities

questions.question: The prepaid insurance of R3 600 is shown:
options: Inside trade and other receivables in current assets

questions.question: If the balance sheet refuses to balance in the examination, the best move is:
options: Change a figure until it balances
Rule it off and move on — follow-on marks protect correct method, and the hunt costs marks elsewhere

questions.question: Tax charge R194 400, SARS owed R9 600 at the start and R14 400 at the end. Tax paid is:
options: R189 600 — charge plus opening owed minus closing owed

questions.question: Dividends paid of R500 000 consists of:
options: This year's interim plus this year's final
Last year's final of R260 000 plus this year's interim of R240 000

questions.question: Opening fixed assets R3 400 000, depreciation R105 000, disposal at carrying value R95 000, closing R3 840 000. Purchases were:
The buy-back appears in financing activities at:
options: Nothing, as buy-backs are not cash
R252 500 — the full price, because that is the cash that left

questions.question: Protea Limited earns 15,4 percent on total capital while loans cost 11 percent. Its 0,7 to 1 gearing is:
options: Justified — each borrowed rand clears 4,4 cents, lifting return on equity above return on capital

questions.question: Aloe Limited earns 9,6 percent on total capital against the same 11 percent loan rate. More borrowing would:
options: Destroy value — each borrowed rand would cost more than it earns, so the low gearing is wise

questions.question: Aloe's current ratio of 3,8 to 1 is best judged as:
options: Ideal — the higher the safer, always
Lazy capital — money sleeping in stock and debtors that could fund expansion or dividends

questions.question: Aloe trades at 510 cents against a net asset value of 560 cents. The discount signals:
options: A printing error in the paper
That the share must be bought immediately
That net asset value is calculated wrongly
Market doubt that the assets will earn their keep — though a bidder might see a bargain

subtopics.title: The Audit Report and Governance Question

questions.question: An unqualified audit opinion states that the financial statements:
options: Fairly present the position and results, in all material respects
Are guaranteed free of any error
Show the company is well managed

questions.question: The audit report is addressed to:
options: The shareholders — the auditors work for the owners, not the managers they check

questions.question: The audit firm also runs the company's bookkeeping. The governance problem is:
options: There is no problem — it saves money
Independence is compromised — the auditors would be checking their own work
The Companies Act requires one firm for both

questions.question: A director buys shares the week before excellent results are announced. This is:
options: Acceptable if the amounts are small
Insider trading — illegal use of knowledge the market lacks
